quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
rationale: Section 15.1 contains a genuine vendor-side indemnity running to us: MSL defends and indemnifies IBM for (a) infringement of any patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work right or trade secret anywhere in the world arising from MSL's performance or MSL-procured parts, processes, designs and pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with law, and (c) MSL's failure to perform its warranty and support obligations. The carve-outs are the usual ones (IBM-selected names/marks, MSL's compliance with IBM's written specifications, defects caused by IBM-supplied designs), and 15.2 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control with our right to participate at our own expense) plus the customary procure-a-licence/redesign remedy in 15.2(b). Section 14 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement is a narrow, loaned-item-only IBM obligation, so there is no broad reciprocal customer indemnity. The clause therefore meets the fallback and substantially the preferred position. Minor sub-elements short of preferred (no express extension to IBM affiliates, no separate limbs for data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, no refund remedy) are noted only. Separately, the 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap in 15.3(b) is expressed to cover "total liability ... regardless of the form of action" and so would bite on this indemnity; that is a limitation-of-liability point and is addressed under the liability rule rather than double-flagged here.

quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

Section 16.5 (Sale or Merger) is favourable to us: it binds only MSL, requiring notice and assumption by any successor, and gives MSL no termination or re-pricing right on an IBM change of control, so no change-of-control right needs deletion; our redline confirms this expressly for the avoidance of doubt. quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
rationale: No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements commitment is imposed on IBM anywhere in the Agreement, which meets the preferred position. Section 3.0 Scope of Work (p0102) simply describes MSL performing "selected manufacturing, Integration, and other Services", and Section 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720) is purchase-order driven ("This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product") rather than a requirements contract; there is no "exclusive", "sole supplier", "all of its requirements" or "shall not procure from any third party" language (searches for "exclusive", "sole", "source", "requirements from", "other suppliers" return only unrelated uses, e.g. MSL's exclusive remedy and MSL buying parts "solely for use in IBM Products", which binds MSL, not us). Product Forecast (p0866) and Supply Flexibility (p0923) create supply-and-demand process and volume-flexibility obligations on MSL and expressly state IBM "will have no liability for unused flexibility", so IBM retains freedom to source elsewhere. The forecast-accuracy charges in Appendix 2 are a volume/forecast-liability point addressed under the applicable commitment rule, not an exclusivity restriction, so no redline is proposed here.

quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. The formulaic amounts payable by IBM under §13.0 f) and Appendix 2 (requirements-accuracy liabilities applied to material cost) and premium-cost reimbursement under §9.0 compensate MSL for actual inventory/premium exposure caused by IBM forecast inaccuracy and are pricing/reimbursement mechanics, not penalties on breach; §13.2 e) expressly confirms IBM has no liability for unused flexibility. quote: IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
rationale: Every licence grant in this deal runs from us (IBM) to MSL, not the other way: § 13.3(a) confirms MSL gets no rights in IBM IP beyond a royalty-free right to use disclosed confidential information solely to manufacture for IBM; § 5 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement licenses Loaned Programs to MSL; Attachment 6 and § 24.1 restrict MSL's use of IBM/third-party software. Those restrictions benefit us and are not flagged. In place of a licence to us, § 13.1 vests outright ownership in IBM (with assignment by MSL) of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of Products delivered and of inventions made on Products and on IBM processes — a position better than the preferred licence scope, since as owner we may extend use to Related Companies and contractors, cannot have rights revoked, and may transfer to successors. Noted but not flagged: § 24.1(a)/(b) state MSL conveys to IBM no licence in MSL or third-party software and neither party gets licence rights or source code without the owner's approval; this is mutual, sits outside the Product IP that we own, and leaves a consent path, so it is not a material licence-scope failure.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience. Section 6.0 makes our purchase obligation subject to the Agreement and expressly does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product absent an order; Section 11.2(d) confirms that forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; Section 6.1 lets us "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (no cancellation charge where MSL is in default); and Section 13.2(e) states we "have no liability for unused flexibility." That matches the preferred position: we pay only for Products actually ordered. The only volume-related exposure is the Appendix 2 / Section 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy mechanism, under which we compensate MSL if forecast accuracy for a machine type falls below the stated threshold, calculated as a small percentage of the material cost of volume shipped. That operates as a capped true-up for MSL's reliance-based parts purchases rather than a shortfall penalty or minimum-volume commitment, so it does not create take-or-pay exposure; we note it in diligence only (the percentages are redacted, so the commercial team should confirm the bracketed figures). No redline required.

ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant, and no redline or comment was proposed — consistent with the playbook's treatment of compliant findings (retained as internal evidence, not raised as a negotiation issue). The cited text supports compliance on the rule's material terms: §5.2(a)(ii) imposes an uncapped obligation on MSL to assist in transferring responsibilities and Products to IBM or its designee (better for us than a 6-month cap), §5.2(a)(iii) requires return of all IBM documentation and confidential media within a defined post-termination window, §13.2(c) permits immediate return on demand, and Attachment 6 §3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic. The rule is a 'missing/insert' rule; since a usable transition-assistance and data-return clause plainly exists, classifying as compliant rather than missing is correct, and inserting the model paragraph would be over-flagging. The failed deterministic check ('data return/transition present') is a phrasing-variant false negative — the quoted paragraphs expressly cover transfer assistance, return of media and certification in non-SaaS 'documentation/media' language rather than 'Customer Data export' wording. Shortfalls versus the model language (no machine-readable-format specification, certification limited to Attachment 6 media, redacted return period) are correctly noted in the rationale as sub-elements rather than escalated to a deviation, with a stated trigger to revisit if the redacted figure materially exceeds 30 days.

ops.text:
16.22 Insurance

MSL shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than one million U.S. dollars (USD 1,000,000) per occurrence and two million U.S. dollars (USD 2,000,000) in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than two million U.S. dollars (USD 2,000,000); (iii) where MSL processes IBM data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than five million U.S. dollars (USD 5,000,000); and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Such coverage is in addition to the insurance required under Section 13.1 b) of the Statement of Work and Section 21.2 of the Statement of Work. MSL shall provide IBM with certificates of insurance upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 16.22 requiring MSL to carry commercial general liability, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation insurance and to provide certificates on request.

quote: MSL will provide replacement value insurance coverage for consigned Products. IBM will be named as a joint insured with respect to consigned Products for its interest.
rationale: There is no insurance clause in the General section (16.1–16.21) or anywhere else in the Base Agreement, Statement of Work or the Loan/Confidentiality attachments. The only insurance-related obligations are narrow property covers: MSL's replacement-value cover for consigned Products (SOW 13.1 b)) and IBM's own cover for its tooling (SOW 21.2, where the insuring party is IBM, not MSL). Section 8 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement actually relieves MSL of risk of loss for Loaned Items. None of this provides commercial general liability, professional liability (E&O) or cyber/privacy cover, so the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is not met on any material term. MSL is a services vendor that occupies IBM-leased premises, handles IBM and IBM-customer inventory and has access to IBM I/T systems, which puts the absence of liability cover in walk-away territory. We have inserted a short insurance paragraph as new Section 16.22 at the playbook's preferred limits, expressly preserving the existing consigned-inventory and tooling cover, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback available in negotiation.

verification.notes: The 'missing' classification is supported: the only insurance provisions in the record are narrow property covers (SOW 13.1 b) replacement-value cover for consigned Products; SOW 21.2 where IBM, not MSL, insures its own tooling), and none of them provides CGL, professional liability or cyber cover, so the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is unmet on every material term — not an acceptable-fallback over-flag. MSL is an outsourcing/services vendor operating at IBM premises and handling IBM consigned inventory, so the rule's expectation of an insurance clause genuinely applies and the absence is actionable. The inserted paragraph tracks the model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where IBM data is processed, workers' compensation, certificates on request, survival for one year) and is an addition only — no existing obligation is altered, and the direction of the edit favours our client (IBM as customer). Comment is accurate, uses the required prefix and tone, states what changed and why, and offers the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present. Minor, non-fatal points to tidy: the insertion is anchored to p0334 (an infringement-remedy paragraph) although it is labelled 16.22 in the General section — confirm it lands after the last 16.x subsection; and the cross-reference calling the new cover 'in addition to the insurance required under Section 21.2' is loose because 21.2 obliges IBM, not MSL, to insure its tooling.
